claims.answer: Podium supports persistent parent and child issues, phases and typed dependency links, including reparenting an existing issue without replacing its identity. Since 0.3.0 issue types are task, phase and decision: epic and other kinds are retired, and any issue with children acts as a parent. Dependency types are fixed to blocked-by, related, discovered-from, supersedes and duplicates. Cycles are refused and docs list an open blocker as a reason an issue cannot start. No mandatory workflow preset applies in the baseline.

claims.answer: v0.3.0 routes Podium issue instructions and relay environment through terminal and engine session launch. Claude stream sessions use appended instructions and boundary callbacks; Codex server sessions use developer instructions, Grok ACP uses rules, and OpenCode uses the prompt system field. Claude and Codex boundary hooks can re-prime after compaction. Transcript mirroring is on by default; full-text indexing needs the command-palette flag, which defaults off. Agent profiles can carry markdown instructions. Curated memory, skills and memory correction or deletion controls remain unestablished. No instruction-delivery or compaction scenario was run.

claims.answer: CLI and MCP address the same canonical issue records for reads, creation, edits, claims, state, dependencies and artifacts. Relayed agents have worker capability scoped to their issue subtree, with --outside-scope confirmation for other existing issues. attachSession is not subtree-gated, but direct rehoming from a real issue is refused and an agent attach naming a Proposed target is refused. That does not make every Proposed subtree inert: operator attachment or spawn-time cwd binding can leave a session attached to a Proposed issue; newSubissue without targetId then bypasses the proposed-parent guard, creates a human-audience backlog child and attaches the existing session. This path remains at v0.3.0 source and was not exercised live. Concurrent-edit handling remains unknown.

permissions.answer: Viewer, worker and admin issue roles exist. A relayed agent receives worker/subtree scope, or none without an issue; --outside-scope confirms other existing-issue writes. Delete and restore are operator-only; only the user closes a decision issue. attachSession is not subtree-gated, but real-issue direct rehoming is refused. Its Proposed guard only checks a supplied targetId for constrained callers. Operator attachment is allowed from a draft session; spawn can persist a Proposed issue attachment through a qualifying cwd when mayJoinIssue passes, because soleOwnerForCwd has no stage filter. Given that attachment, newSubissue with no targetId and confirmRehome creates a human-audience backlog child and attaches the session, bypassing registry create protections. This is a source path, not a verified live exploit.

claims.answer: Podium exposes retryable errors, optional auto-continue with backoff, bounded waits and provider quota. Claude stream and hosted headless drivers enforce a supplied turn deadline, with no deadline when timeoutMs is absent. The one-shot headless server runner supplies its budget, default ten minutes. Agent spawns have a daily per-issue budget. Operator-configurable task-wide turn, token and spend caps remain unestablished; quota display is not enforcement.

timeouts.answer: agent await is bounded (30s default, 300s max); managed-session approvals wait up to 10 minutes; the default shipping validation has a 10 minute timeout. retries.answer: Auto-continue types continue into retryable-errored sessions with backoff from 10 seconds to 5 minutes when the global switch is on; default off.

claims.answer: Docs state repositories and native harness credentials stay on machines you control and server state lives in a documented directory. Since 0.2.0 a daily usage report is on by default and can be turned off; crash reports stay opt-in. Usage reports carry an install id, schema version, Podium version, OS, architecture, bucketed install age and machine count, session counts per harness and whether issues were used. Crash reports carry the same install id, versions, OS and architecture, a fixed error type and up to 20 stack frames, each with a Podium source file path, line and function when there is one; error messages and frames outside Podium are dropped. evidence.title: Podium SECURITY.md
evidence.finding: Vulnerabilities are reported privately via GitHub Security Advisories or email; acknowledgement within 7 days is stated; only the latest release and main get fixes; server is designed for loopback or an authenticated proxy; agent sessions execute real shell commands.

evidence.title: Podium telemetry contract
evidence.locator: Short version; What is sent; Where it goes; Who sends
evidence.finding: Usage reports are on by default and sent once a day; crash reports are off unless turned on. Nothing is asked during setup. Fields are a fixed schema that excludes paths, prompts, transcripts and code. The relay drops IP addresses and forwards to PostHog Cloud. Settings, Privacy, podium telemetry off, DO_NOT_TRACK=1 and PODIUM_TELEMETRY=off turn reports off. The first report goes out about a minute after first start.

evidence.title: Run coding agents with Podium
evidence.finding: Docs home: Podium runs native Claude Code, Codex, Grok, OpenCode, Cursor and Pi processes on machines you control; supported core is a local or self-hosted control system; built first for one operator supervising several agents. Its Windows matrix wording is superseded by v0.3.0 assets.

evidence.title: Check feature availability
evidence.locator: Supported core; Conditional; Preview; Experimental; Hosted
evidence.finding: Separates supported core, conditional paths, preview clients, experimental features and unconfirmed hosted behavior. Page text predates 0.2.0: it still says Windows packaging is disabled in the default release matrix and calls usage telemetry opt-in, both superseded by the v0.3.0 release assets and telemetry source. Billing, hosted metering and retention controls are still listed as not implemented.

evidence.title: Install and set up Podium
evidence.locator: Choose a supported deployment; First-run setup; Remote access
evidence.finding: Install paths: macOS desktop, headless Linux x86_64 and ARM64, Linux AppImage preview, Windows experimental, hosted Podium unconfirmed. Setup registers a Git repository, detects harness login and supports Tailscale, Cloudflare quick tunnel or reverse proxy. Its opt-in telemetry step and Windows pipeline wording are superseded at v0.3.0.

evidence.title: Complete your first issue
evidence.finding: Documented first-task loop: podium status, issue create, issue start --agent (creates branch and worktree), follow with issue show and session status, review evidence, close or merge. Requires a configured instance, a registered Git repository and one installed, authenticated harness.

evidence.title: Understand how Podium runs agents
evidence.finding: Server owns issues, sessions, artifacts; a daemon on each machine launches harnesses in real pseudo-terminals and connects outward; clients attach to live terminals and disconnecting does not end the session.

evidence.title: Understand issues, sessions, agents, and harnesses
evidence.finding: Issues are durable work records separate from sessions; one issue can retain several sessions; stopping a process hibernates a resumable session keeping transcript and branch; harness capabilities differ by harness.

evidence.title: Understand repositories, worktrees, and machines
evidence.finding: Repositories are registered per machine and can be cloned from a cloneable origin into ~/podium-repos; issues own a branch and linked worktree; Podium will not resolve branch conflicts; workspace fetch exposes another agent files read-only across machines.

evidence.title: Create and track issue work
evidence.locator: Create; Start or claim; State and todos; Dependencies; Close
evidence.finding: CLI for creating, starting, planning, claiming, stating, todos, dependencies, spinoff attach and closing; agent-filed top-level issues land in proposed; operator-created issues start in backlog. Its --type blocks example is refused at v0.3.0, where the type is blocked-by.

evidence.title: Delegate work to other agents
evidence.locator: Work shapes; spawn; child issue; mail; leases
evidence.finding: Delegation shapes: another session on the same issue, child issue with its own worktree, or discovered-from top-level issue; podium agent spawn/status/await; durable mail with optional expected response; advisory lock leases. States Podium does not serialize agents editing one worktree.

evidence.title: Review and accept agent work
evidence.locator: Move to review; Check; Offer; Accept
evidence.finding: Review path: issue artifacts, stage review, diff and checks, podium offer buttons, merge under merge-lock, issue action merge closes the issue; feedback keeps it open. Its rule that artifact sources sit inside the issue worktree is superseded at v0.3.0.

evidence.title: Supervise a running agent session
evidence.locator: Status; Read; Send; Stop; Attention states
evidence.finding: Supervision commands: session status/read/recap/send (--wake)/continue/stop; stop refuses a dirty managed worktree unless forced; attention states (needs input, idle, working, retryable error, permission request).

evidence.title: Add a remote machine
evidence.finding: Settings, Machines, Add machine creates a single-use hour-long pairing install command for a Linux host; verify with machine list/show/reprobe; place issues with issue start --machine; portable session handoff is not baseline stable.

evidence.title: Use the Podium CLI
evidence.finding: Stable command groups: lifecycle, work (issue, session, agent, mail, offer, worktree, workspace, lock, merge-lock), machines and access (machine, auth, quota, telemetry). Workflow, spec, automation, notification, shipping and handoff commands are behind default-off flags and not baseline.

evidence.title: Configure a Podium installation
evidence.locator: State root; Operator keys; Environment overrides
evidence.finding: State lives in ~/.podium; modes all-in-one, server, daemon, client, supervisor; transcriptLake default on; unlisted PODIUM_* variables are not a public contract. Its telemetry.usage default is superseded at v0.3.0: absent usage counts as on.

evidence.title: Reference issue and session states
evidence.locator: Issue stages; Session states; Dependency meanings
evidence.finding: Issue stages proposed, backlog, planning, in_progress, review, shipping, done; session states working, idle, needs input, permission needed, retryable error, hibernated; close reasons. Its dependency list (blocks, tracks, caused-by, validates) is superseded by the fixed v0.3.0 list in v030-vocab.

evidence.title: Protect Podium data and credentials
evidence.locator: Pairing; Stored data; Review agent actions; Telemetry; Website analytics
evidence.finding: Daemons connect outward; pairing codes expire in one hour and copy Claude Code and Codex credentials only when enabled; artifacts are immutable server copies; lifecycle commands and automation requests may need operator approval; harnesses run with host account permissions; hosted PostHog and website Google Analytics and Ads are separate paths. Its statement that self-hosted telemetry is opt-in is superseded at v0.3.0 by telemetry-doc and v030-consent.

evidence.title: Update and back up Podium
evidence.finding: Backups are a stopped copy of the state root; Podium writes a database-only migration snapshot (three retained) before migrations; updater verifies release signatures; an epoch-safe restore exists but is not wired to a shipped command.

evidence.title: Troubleshoot Podium by layer
evidence.locator: First checks; Issue cannot start; Diagnostics
evidence.finding: Layered troubleshooting; an issue cannot start if blocked by an open dependency, machine offline, repository absent, harness not logged in, or worktree conflict; crash export command.

evidence.title: Podium apps/cli/src/agent-cli.ts
evidence.finding: podium agent spawn starts a full Podium session (real PTY, visible in the UI) on an issue with --harness, --model, --effort and new --profile; the caller becomes parent; await is bounded (default 30s, max 300s). Help lists claude-code, codex, grok, opencode and cursor; it does not list pi, while the harness enum does.

evidence.title: Podium apps/cli/src/session-cli.ts
evidence.locator: help text: send, continue, status, read, recap, handoff, stop
evidence.finding: Session CLI: send (--wake queues and resumes a parked session), continue (errored phase only), status (no transcript text), read, recap, ask, title, handoff to another machine (target must be online; harness must support it), stop (frees worktree, keeps branch).

evidence.title: Podium apps/server/src/mcp-route.ts
evidence.finding: Server exposes a minimal stateless tools-only MCP endpoint over HTTP JSON-RPC (initialize, tools/list, tools/call), bearer-token gated, intended for loopback use by harness agents.

evidence.title: Podium apps/server/src/issue-mcp.ts
evidence.finding: Issue MCP tools are generated from the shared ISSUE_COMMANDS registry as issue_<command> tools, so CLI and MCP operate on the same issue commands.

evidence.title: Podium automations/decide.ts
evidence.finding: Pure scheduler decision: occurrences more than one hour late are recorded missed and not backfilled; an automation whose previous session is still live is skipped as overlap; otherwise a session is spawned.

evidence.title: Podium automations/scheduler.ts
evidence.finding: Server-owned scheduler ticks every 30 seconds after a 20 second boot delay, single-flight, inert until an enabled automation exists; schedule kinds are cron and once (model automation.ts line 48).

evidence.title: Podium approvals/service.ts
evidence.finding: Approval broker: agents request management operations through the relay, the operator approves or denies, the owning daemon executes, every step is appended to the issue activity log and the outcome is mailed to the agent; pending approvals are durable rows with no timeout.

evidence.title: Podium apps/cli/src/approval-cli.ts
evidence.finding: Inside a managed session, management commands block up to 10 minutes for an operator decision; denied or failed requests exit nonzero; on timeout the request stays valid and the outcome arrives as issue mail.

evidence.title: Podium packages/model/src/authz/issue-authz.ts
evidence.finding: Issue authorization policy defines viewer, worker and admin roles mapped to read, write and manage actions with closed scope kinds (all, none, subtree, owned, self). Source comment at lines 58-62 says the current scope is all and subtree is the reserved per-issue extension. The operator is unconstrained and agents carry a constrained capability. Commands carry actor and on-behalf-of fields.

evidence.title: Podium apps/server/src/auto-continue.ts
evidence.finding: When a global master switch is on, sessions in a retryable errored phase receive continue on escalating backoff from 10 seconds to a 5 minute cap until they recover.

evidence.title: Podium packages/model/src/settings/preferences.ts
evidence.finding: Settings defaults: auto-continue off; worktree GC mode propose after 14 days; git workflow mergeStyle ff-only, pr or ask (default ff-only) and autoRebaseBeforeMerge default true.

evidence.title: Podium apps/daemon/src/repo-op.ts
evidence.finding: Daemon repo operations include a guarded gh pr create --base <parent> --head <branch> --fill, used by the issue action pr.

evidence.title: Podium apps/web/src/features/usage/UsageView.tsx
evidence.finding: Usage and analytics sheet shows what the machine agents spent at hour resolution over seven days, leading with list-price cost, with a quota ledger and per-task costs.

evidence.title: Podium apps/cli/src/quota-cli.ts

evidence.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/memory/lake.ts

evidence.title: Podium packages/harness/src/driver/families/terminal/runtime.ts

evidence.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/superagent/headless.ts

evidence.title: Podium packages/harness/src/driver/families/headless/turn.ts
evidence.finding: Hosted headless turns enforce a supplied timeoutMs; absent timeoutMs does not arm a turn deadline. Other lifecycle, provider and explicit-call limits remain separate.

evidence.title: Public pricing search

evidence.title: GitHub tag object for v0.3.0
evidence.finding: Public annotated tag ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5 peels to commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, tagged 2026-11-05. The local read-only clone resolves v0.3.0 to the same commit, and 81 cited or sampled files matched raw.githubusercontent.com byte for byte.

evidence.title: Podium v0.3.0 release
evidence.finding: Stable release published 2026-11-05: flight deck, calmer chat and workspace, reduced server memory and more reliable updates. Assets include macOS arm64 and x64 dmg, Linux amd64 AppImage, Windows x64-setup.exe, headless bundles for darwin and linux (arm64 and x64), install.sh and SHA256SUMS. The memory figures in the notes are the vendor benchmark, not an independent result.

evidence.title: Podium v0.2.0 release
evidence.locator: Release body: What's new; Upgrading from 0.1.0
evidence.finding: Stable release: more reliable chat, cost per task on the task header and usage sheet, Pi fully supported, improved mobile app, experimental Windows and Linux desktop builds, updates that show progress and roll back on failure. Sessions running during the upgrade keep running on the old terminal host.

evidence.title: Server data access measurement
evidence.finding: Vendor bench behind the 0.3.0 memory note. On a 4 CPU, 12 GB VM, server RSS was 326 MiB on a 4,867-issue corpus and 334 MiB on a 27,601-issue corpus, against 457 and 1,188 MiB before; boot to listen was 8% and 52% faster. SQL statements rose about 30%. The document says its live half was pending. Not reproduced by this research pass.

evidence.title: Podium apps/web/src/app/FlightDeck.tsx
evidence.finding: Flight deck UI renders one mission: phases, tasks, seats, proposals and a cost chip, with sibling files for dependencies, seats and groups. No feature flag gates it. AppShell binds the toggle.

evidence.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/issues/service/deck.ts
evidence.finding: Server deck snapshot rolls task state words and counts up from leaf tasks and joins seats, blockers and proposals. Rollup is a derived view; hierarchy.ts notes a phase never closes by itself.

evidence.title: Podium packages/issue-client/src/deck.ts
evidence.finding: podium issue deck prints the same snapshot: counts by state, phases, tasks, session seats with harness, model and effort, unmet blockers and proposals.

evidence.title: Podium packages/model/src/entities/issue-vocabulary.ts
evidence.finding: Issue types are task, phase and decision. Epic, milestone, automation, bug, feature, chore, story and spike are retired, with labels replacing the kind words. Only the user closes a decision. Dependency types are fixed to blocked-by, related, discovered-from, supersedes and duplicates, with a CHECK constraint.

evidence.title: Podium packages/telemetry/src/consent.ts
evidence.finding: Absent usage consent counts as on; absent crash consent counts as off. An explicit off stays off. The comment dates opt-out usage reports to 0.2.0.

evidence.title: Podium packages/harness/src/adapters/pi/index.ts
evidence.locator: capabilities 126; quota false; handoff false; hookInstall none; instrumentation unsupported
evidence.finding: Pi adapter launches the native CLI with create-or-resume sessions and thinking levels as effort, and reads its stream for state. It declares no quota, no handoff and no hooks, and it does not declare queuesBusyInput.

evidence.title: Podium packages/model/src/entities/agent-profile.ts
evidence.finding: Agent profiles are named setups with ordered harness, model and effort candidates, an optional machine and markdown instructions. The first usable candidate is picked at session start, and sessions do not switch harness mid-run. Import and export use a Claude Code agent file at .podium/agents/<name>.md. People edit profiles; agents can only pick one.

evidence.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/issues/service/seat.ts
evidence.finding: A session seat decides whether it may talk to the user or must ask a coordinator. Below-coordinator sessions are pointed at issue mail.

evidence.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/messages/handlers/spawn-agent.ts
evidence.finding: Agent-initiated spawns take a budget of 10 per target issue per UTC day, shared with mail-triggered spawns. Human-principal spawns are exempt.

evidence.title: Podium apps/server/src/member-routes.ts
evidence.finding: Member routes list members, create invites and change or remove membership, and answer 403 unless the actor has the admin role.

evidence.title: Podium apps/web/src/features/settings/sections/members.tsx
evidence.finding: Settings has a Members section with invite links, optional invitation email, member or admin role and member removal. Which installs reach it and how it behaves were not tested.

evidence.title: Podium apps/web/src/features/files/artifacts-tab.ts
evidence.finding: Artifacts group as screens (images and video), documents and reports, with filter chips and search in ArtifactsTab.tsx.

evidence.title: Podium apps/web/src/features/issues/IssuesFilters.tsx
evidence.finding: The issue board has a filter control alongside CLI search by text, status, priority, type and label.

evidence.title: Podium apps/web/src/features/issues/board-shortcuts.ts
evidence.finding: Board keys cover j/k and arrow movement, x to select, Enter to open, c to create, four property menus and a ? help sheet.

evidence.title: Podium apps/web/src/features/usage/UsageTasks.tsx
evidence.finding: The usage sheet lists per-task costs from the same token records.

evidence.title: Podium apps/server/src/store.ts
evidence.finding: The command-palette flag decides at boot whether full-text indexing of conversations and transcripts exists. It is edge-visibility and default off; with it off, search falls back to LIKE.

evidence.title: Podium apps/server/src/issue-authz.ts
evidence.finding: The server gate refuses a constrained capability writing an existing issue outside its subtree unless --outside-scope is passed. A scope of all returns without a subtree check.

evidence.title: Podium apps/server/src/relay.ts
evidence.finding: The spec pointer is registered with featureEnabled(specs), so agents are told about the spec CLI only with the flag on.

evidence.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/issues/service/workflow.ts
evidence.finding: issue action pr records the URL printed by gh on the issue as prUrl.

evidence.title: Podium install.sh
evidence.finding: The headless installer installs missing prerequisites through apt and other supported package managers, or stops with a message when none is found.

evidence.title: Podium .github/workflows/desktop-release.yml
evidence.finding: The desktop release workflow includes a windows-x86_64 target, matching the x64-setup.exe asset in v0.3.0.

evidence.title: Podium docs: security and privacy
evidence.locator: Control self-hosted telemetry; page footer last modified November 6, 2026
evidence.finding: Live page now says a self-hosted host sends one anonymous usage report a day unless turned off, the default since 0.2.0, and that setup does not ask.

evidence.title: Podium docs: install
evidence.locator: Platform table; first-run steps; page footer last modified November 6, 2026
evidence.finding: Live page now says setup does not ask about telemetry, usage reports are on by default and crash reports off. Windows desktop is Experimental; a release can publish without it.

evidence.title: Podium docs: feature availability
evidence.locator: Supported core; Preview or unsupported clients; page footer last modified November 6, 2026
evidence.finding: Live page lists usage reports on by default and crash reports opt-in, says each release also builds an experimental Windows x64 installer, and still says reviewed sources do not confirm native iPhone distribution.

evidence.title: Podium docs: lifecycle
evidence.locator: Dependency types; page footer last modified November 6, 2026
evidence.finding: Live page documents blocked-by as the default dependency type and the only type that makes an issue blocked; the blocks type is no longer shown.

evidence.title: Podium v0.3.1 release
evidence.finding: Stable v0.3.1, published 2026-11-06, lists one change: fixed update failures in rare configurations. The diff from v0.3.0 is desktop payload startup, client registration and Codex rollout recovery; features.ts, packages/telemetry and docs/TELEMETRY.md are unchanged.

evidence.title: Podium apps/daemon/src/repo-op.ts
evidence.finding: The daemon clone operation runs git clone -- <originUrl> <path>. In this file only prCreate uses gh.

evidence.title: Podium telemetry contract, report tiers
evidence.locator: What is sent: usage, crash; What is never sent, at any tier
evidence.finding: Usage reports carry schema, installId, version, os, arch, bucketed installAge and machines, session counts per harness and whether issues were used. Crash reports carry schema, installId, version, os, arch, a fixed errorType and up to 20 frames, each a path inside the Podium source tree, a line and a function when there is one. Crash reports carry Podium source lines, so they are off unless turned on. Error messages and frames outside the Podium install are dropped. The never-sent list names filesystem paths, repo names, prompts, transcripts and your code, so it does not cover the Podium source paths in crash frames. This refines the telemetry-doc record.

evidence.title: Podium packages/telemetry/src/schema.ts
evidence.finding: The report schema defines usage reports with sessions and features records, and stack frames with file, line and optional fn. Crash reports hold at most 20 frames.

evidence.title: Podium configuration reference, Podium Connect
evidence.finding: PODIUM_CONNECT defaults to on. A server with a public URL registers its installation id and public key once with connect.podium.do, then publishes that URL on start, on change, after a transfer and daily. Nothing is sent before a public URL exists. Off clears the published record and stops. The live configuration page retrieved 2026-11-06 does not mention Connect.

evidence.title: Podium public guide: reference/feature-availability
evidence.finding: Hosted production cutover is unconfirmed; hosted workspace requests create pending records requiring manual provisioning. Billing, hosted metering and durable cloud lifecycle are not implemented product claims. Experimental workflows/specs/automations/shipping are not baseline.

evidence.title: Podium v0.3.0: apps/server/src/mcp-route.ts
evidence.finding: The accessible /mcp server accepts tools-only JSON-RPC POST behind a bearer/x-podium-mcp-token, with opaque per-thread identity and fail-closed start-capable tool calls. This is an MCP server, not proof of an external MCP client registry.

evidence.title: Podium v0.3.0: docs/agents/podium-specs.md
evidence.locator: Write what humans decide; stable IDs and reference format
evidence.finding: Experimental specs guidance permits only explicit human decisions/context and directs an agent to flag contradictions, mark superseded decisions and retain stable SP references. This is agent guidance, not an enforced approval or drift-detection engine.

evidence.title: Podium v0.3.0: apps/server/src/modules/superagent/tools.ts
evidence.finding: Assistant tools expose ranked internal sessions/issues/comments/conversation/transcript/settings results with identifiers and snippets. Conversation/full-text search tools are removed when the default-off command-palette flag leaves indexing disabled. They do not search repository code or external knowledge.

evidence.title: Podium v0.3.0: apps/server/src/modules/automations/service.ts
evidence.finding: Scheduler records occurrence outcomes spawned/error/missed/skipped_overlap; nextRunAt re-arms after spawn attempt success or terminal error. Resume may fall back to fresh only for missing durable session or resume ref. Outcome spawned is not verified task completion.

evidence.title: Podium v0.3.0: apps/server/src/modules/events/retention.ts
evidence.finding: The event-retention service prunes podium_events older than14 days or beyond50000 rows, initially60seconds after boot then every6hours, bounded500row batches. Server relay constructs and starts it; this is separate from issue/comment/transcript retention.

evidence.title: Podium v0.3.0: apps/server/src/relay.ts
evidence.finding: The release relay constructs EventLogRetention on store.events and registers its lifecycle. This connects retention to the shipped server rather than an isolated helper.

evidence.title: Podium public guide: guides/review-work
evidence.locator: Check the deliverable; Present one decision; Accept or return the work
evidence.finding: Review guide walks acceptance criteria/state, Git diffs, validation, artifacts and caveats, then an offer with merge and send-back feedback actions. This is single-issue guidance, not a measured six-task batch review.

evidence.title: Podium public guide: security/privacy
evidence.locator: Keep the server boundary small; Protect machine pairing
evidence.finding: Daemon connects outbound; remote route should use TLS/private Tailscale. One-time pairing codes expire after one hour; native Claude/Codex credential copying is explicit per grant. This is access/pairing, not command sandboxing.

evidence.title: Podium apps/server/src/relay.ts
evidence.locator: lines 3905-3907 (event-log retention timer retired) and 3932-3934 (automations scheduler timer retired)
evidence.finding: At v0.3.0 the relay still constructs EventLogRetention and AutomationScheduler but no longer starts them. Comments mark both timers as retired: the janitor owns event-log pruning and automation fires.

evidence.title: Podium apps/server/src/janitor-host.ts
evidence.locator: header comment lines 1-21; startJanitorHost line 60 (called from server.ts 2118)
evidence.finding: The janitor runs in a worker thread owned by the server process, and the server always starts it. It reads the database read-only and writes through the server's maintenance routes.

evidence.title: Podium packages/janitor/src/janitor.ts
evidence.locator: DEFAULT_TICK_MS line 63; HOUSEKEEPING_EVERY_TICKS line 66; housekeeping jobs 323-333; runEventLogPrune 365; runAutomationFires 511
evidence.finding: The janitor ticks every 30 seconds by default. Each housekeeping tick runs event-log pruning, using the age and row limits from the server lease, and applies due automation fires, among other jobs.

evidence.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/automations/service.ts
evidence.finding: The janitor's fenced automation-fire job calls applyObservedOccurrence. The server revalidates the schedule and runs the same decideTick policy (grace, overlap, re-arm) before it spawns.

evidence.title: Podium packages/protocol/src/maintenance.ts
evidence.locator: EVENT_RETENTION_MAX_AGE_DAYS, EVENT_RETENTION_MAX_ROWS, EVENT_PRUNE_BATCH_ROWS lines 45-47 (served in the lease by apps/server/src/modules/maintenance/service.ts 152-153)
evidence.finding: The maintenance protocol fixes event-log retention at 14 days and 50,000 rows with 500-row prune batches. The server hands these limits to the janitor in its maintenance lease.

evidence.title: Podium: Three ways to use Podium; Every app connects to every Podium
evidence.locator: Three ways to use Podium; Every app connects to every Podium
evidence.finding: The complete published execution choices are the user computer and the user VPS. Phone and browser clients connect to either one; the download page offers no Podium-operated execution host. Its phone choices are a phone browser and a native iPhone private beta, with no native Android client.

evidence.title: Podium: packages/pty/src/backends/index.ts
evidence.locator: defaultPtyBackend; bun-terminal-backend.ts; apps/daemon/src session launch paths
evidence.finding: The released terminal backend launches native harness processes through the host PTY. Inspection of the daemon launch paths and packages/pty for Docker, Podman, container, microVM, QEMU and Firecracker provisioning found no product-managed container or VM isolation. Git worktree separation and provider/host permissions are separate.

evidence.title: Podium: apps/server/src/auth-route.ts
evidence.locator: ClientSessionStore, password verification, native-client and cookie/bearer session routes; member-routes.ts
evidence.finding: The released client authentication routes use password-backed member sessions, cookies and paired mobile bearer tokens. Bounded inspection of the server authentication and membership code for SAML/OIDC/SSO found no enterprise single sign-on path. Coding-agent provider OAuth logins are separate.

podium:PLAN-07.answer: Public CLI and MCP source call the issue service for canonical issue IDs: create, update, claim, state, todos, comments, parent relationships, dependencies and artifacts. A relayed agent session is scoped to the subtree of its own issue (or to no issue when it has none): writing an existing issue outside that scope is refused once and needs --outside-scope to confirm, while reads and creating new issues are unrestricted. Exception: attachSession, which re-homes the agent session onto another issue, is deliberately not scope-gated and needs no --outside-scope. Agents cannot attach a session to a proposed issue; creating a sub-issue under a proposed parent is allowed, and that sub-issue is kept inert (not started). The operator and web are unconstrained. This is present in the v0.1.0 source and at main d3d67cf. Concurrent-edit handling and live behavior were not tested; concurrent-edit handling is unknown.

permissions.answer: Roles are viewer, worker and admin. A relayed agent session is a worker scoped to its own issue subtree (none if issueless): an edit outside it is refused once unless --outside-scope is given; delete and restore are operator-only. The exception is attachSession, deliberately not scope-gated (registry.ts v0.1.0 649-668; main 717-745), so an agent can re-home its session outside its subtree without --outside-scope; agents cannot attach to proposed issues, while creating a sub-issue under a proposed parent is allowed and kept inert (registry.ts create handler, v0.1.0 near 523-565). Enforced in server code at v0.1.0 and main d3d67cf; not exercised in a live session. The "scope is all today" comment in packages/model/src/authz/issue-authz.ts (lines 58-70) is stale: the code governs, and session-authz capabilityForSession mints subtree or none scope for relayed agents.

contradictions: Attach anchor: attachSession with newSubissue and no targetId files the child under the session's current issue (prevId) and re-homes the session onto it (attention.ts v0.1.0 153-187; main 161-187). The proposed-issue check runs only on input.targetId (registry.ts v0.1.0 658-661; main 726-729), so a session already bound to a proposed issue can mint a human-audience child under it without the proposed check, unlike the create handler, which keeps such a child audience agent. The answer's "kept inert" and "agents cannot attach a session to a proposed issue" are therefore not established for this path. Reachability (session bound to a proposed issue via explicit attachment or working directory, session-authz.ts 172-190) is not established.

podium:PLAN-07.answer: CLI and MCP address the same canonical issue records for reads, creation, edits, claims, state, dependencies and artifacts. Relayed agents have worker capability scoped to their issue subtree, with --outside-scope confirmation for other existing issues. attachSession is not subtree-gated, but direct rehoming from a real issue is refused and an agent attach naming a Proposed target is refused. That does not make every Proposed subtree inert: operator attachment or spawn-time cwd binding can leave a session explicitly attached to a Proposed issue; newSubissue without targetId then bypasses the proposed-parent guard, creates a human-audience backlog child with startNow false, and attaches the existing session. This path exists in both public v0.1.0 and current main source. It was not exercised live. Concurrent-edit handling remains unknown.

results.answer: artifact add/get operations and close with completion note.

human_visibility.answer: The public site says agents and the operator use the same board, and its team view shows agent contributions; the view was not tested.

attribution.answer: The authorization model carries an actor and an on-behalf-of principal on commands, and issue activity is logged. Attribution display on the issue page was not established.

permissions.answer: Viewer, worker and admin issue roles exist. A relayed agent receives worker/subtree scope, or none without an issue; --outside-scope confirms other existing-issue writes. Delete/restore are operator-only. attachSession is not subtree-gated, but real-issue direct rehoming is refused. Its Proposed guard only checks a supplied targetId for constrained callers. Operator attachment is allowed from a draft/unbound session; spawn can persist a Proposed issue attachment through a qualifying cwd because soleOwnerForCwd has no stage filter. Given that explicit attachment, newSubissue with no targetId and confirmRehome creates a human-facing backlog child and attaches the session, bypassing registry create protections. A qualifying cwd must have an existing recorded unique deepest non-archived worktree outside registered repository roots; an ordinary new proposal has no such worktree. Current main and public v0.1.0 have this source path, not a verified live exploit. Current main also has an overridable working-session close guard.

limitations: Source reachability established independently for public v0.1.0 and current main. No live attachment, child creation or enforcement test was performed.

Direct agent attach --id to a Proposed target is blocked. Operator attachment and qualifying spawn-time cwd ownership are different entry routes. A bare cwd capability fallback does not itself provide attachSession with prevId; the session must acquire a persisted explicit attachment.

newSubissue sets startNow false, so it does not spawn another process. It attaches the already-existing session to a human-audience backlog child, which is why it cannot be described as universally inert. Other active sessions may require a replacement coordinator.
Current main adds a confirmInterrupt override for working-session close; it does not fix the proposed-parent attach path. Concurrent-edit handling and attribution-display behavior remain untested.

telemetry-doc.title: Podium telemetry contract
telemetry-doc.locator: Short version; What is sent; Where it goes; Who sends
telemetry-doc.finding: Telemetry is off by default, asked once at the end of podium setup, sends at most one daily usage report and rate-limited crash reports with fixed-schema fields, never paths, prompts, transcripts or code, drops IP at a Podium-operated relay, forwards to PostHog Cloud, and is disabled by DO_NOT_TRACK=1 or PODIUM_TELEMETRY=off.

doc-home.title: Run coding agents with Podium
doc-home.finding: Docs home: Podium runs native Claude Code, Codex, Grok, OpenCode, Cursor and Pi processes on machines you control; supported core is a local or self-hosted control system; packaged desktop supports macOS, headless bundles Linux x86_64/ARM64, Linux AppImage preview, Windows experimental and not in the default release matrix; built first for one operator supervising several agents.

doc-availability.title: Check feature availability
doc-availability.locator: Supported core; Conditional; Preview; Experimental; Hosted
doc-availability.finding: Separates supported core (macOS desktop incl. Intel, headless Linux, issues, dependencies, worktrees, artifacts, offers, mail, multi-machine pairing, file browsing, stable/edge channels, opt-in telemetry) from conditional paths, preview clients (Linux AppImage; Windows experimental; native iPhone not confirmed; /mobile web build unsupported), experimental features (cloud runtimes, workflows, specs, automations, notifications, queues, shipping, handoff) and unconfirmed hosted behavior (billing, metering, retention controls not implemented).

doc-install.title: Install and set up Podium
doc-install.locator: Choose a supported deployment; First-run setup; Remote access
doc-install.finding: Install paths: macOS desktop (Apple silicon and Intel), headless Linux x86_64/ARM64 via signed installer, Linux AppImage preview, Windows experimental, hosted Podium unconfirmed. Setup registers a Git repository, detects installed harnesses and login state, offers a telemetry choice, and supports Tailscale, Cloudflare quick tunnel or reverse proxy access.

doc-quickstart.title: Complete your first issue
doc-quickstart.finding: Documented first-task loop: podium status, issue create, issue start --agent (creates branch and worktree), follow with issue show and session status, review evidence, close or merge. Requires a configured instance, a registered Git repository and one installed, authenticated harness.

doc-how.title: Understand how Podium runs agents
doc-how.finding: Server owns issues, sessions, artifacts; a daemon on each machine launches harnesses in real pseudo-terminals and connects outward; clients attach to live terminals and disconnecting does not end the session; mobile clients expose attention, issues, sessions and terminals but native iPhone release is not confirmed.

doc-agents.title: Understand issues, sessions, agents, and harnesses
doc-agents.finding: Issues are durable work records separate from sessions; one issue can retain several sessions; stopping a process hibernates a resumable session keeping transcript and branch; harness capabilities differ by harness.

doc-workspaces.title: Understand repositories, worktrees, and machines
doc-workspaces.finding: Repositories are registered per machine and can be cloned from a cloneable origin into ~/podium-repos; issues own a branch and linked worktree; Podium will not resolve branch conflicts; workspace fetch exposes another agent files read-only across machines.

doc-create.title: Create and track issue work
doc-create.locator: Create; Start or claim; State and todos; Dependencies; Close
doc-create.finding: CLI for creating, starting, planning, claiming, stating, todo checkpoints, blocking and discovered-from dependencies, spinoff attach and closing; agent-filed top-level issues land in proposed; operator-created issues start in backlog.

doc-delegate.title: Delegate work to other agents
doc-delegate.locator: Work shapes; spawn; child issue; mail; leases
doc-delegate.finding: Delegation shapes: another session on the same issue, child issue with its own worktree, or discovered-from top-level issue; podium agent spawn/status/await; durable mail with optional expected response; advisory lock leases. States Podium does not serialize agents editing one worktree.

doc-review.title: Review and accept agent work
doc-review.locator: Move to review; Check; Offer; Accept
doc-review.finding: Review path: issue artifacts, stage review, diff and checks, podium offer buttons, merge under merge-lock, issue action merge closes the issue; feedback action keeps it open.

doc-supervise.title: Supervise a running agent session
doc-supervise.locator: Status; Read; Send; Stop; Attention states
doc-supervise.finding: Supervision commands: session status/read/recap/send (--wake)/continue/stop; stop refuses a dirty managed worktree unless forced; attention states (needs input, idle, working, retryable error, permission request).

doc-machine.title: Add a remote machine
doc-machine.finding: Settings, Machines, Add machine creates a single-use hour-long pairing install command for a Linux host; verify with machine list/show/reprobe; place issues with issue start --machine; portable session handoff is not baseline stable.

doc-cli.title: Use the Podium CLI
doc-cli.finding: Stable command groups: lifecycle (setup, status, stop, logs, update, channel), work (issue, session, agent, mail, offer, worktree, workspace, lock, merge-lock), machines and access (machine, auth, quota, telemetry). Workflow, spec, automation, notification, shipping and handoff commands are behind default-off flags and not baseline.

doc-config.title: Configure a Podium installation
doc-config.locator: State root; Operator keys; Environment overrides
doc-config.finding: State (SQLite database, uploads, transcripts, artifacts, logs, daemon identity) lives in ~/.podium; modes all-in-one/server/daemon/client/supervisor; telemetry keys off unless enabled; transcriptLake default on; unlisted PODIUM_* variables are not a public contract.

doc-lifecycle.title: Reference issue and session states
doc-lifecycle.locator: Issue stages; Session states; Dependency meanings
doc-lifecycle.finding: Issue stages proposed/backlog/planning/in_progress/review/shipping/done; session states working/idle/needs input/permission needed/retryable error/hibernated; close reasons; defined dependency types blocks, related, parent-child, discovered-from, tracks, supersedes, caused-by, validates.

doc-privacy.title: Protect Podium data and credentials
doc-privacy.locator: Pairing; Stored data; Review agent actions; Telemetry; Website analytics
doc-privacy.finding: Daemons connect outward; pairing codes expire in one hour and can copy Claude Code and Codex credentials only when enabled; artifacts are immutable server copies; lifecycle commands and automation requests may need operator approval; harnesses run with host account permissions; telemetry opt-in; hosted app PostHog and website Google Analytics are separate paths.

doc-update.title: Update and back up Podium
doc-update.finding: Backups are a stopped copy of the state root; Podium writes a database-only migration snapshot (three retained) before migrations; updater verifies release signatures; an epoch-safe restore exists in the build but is not wired to a shipped command.

doc-trouble.title: Troubleshoot Podium by layer
doc-trouble.locator: First checks; Issue cannot start; Diagnostics
doc-trouble.finding: Layered troubleshooting; an issue cannot start if blocked by an open dependency, machine offline, repository absent, harness not logged in, or worktree conflict; crash export command.

src-agent-cli.title: Podium apps/cli/src/agent-cli.ts
src-agent-cli.finding: podium agent spawn starts a full Podium session (real PTY, visible in the UI) on an issue with --harness claude-code|codex|grok|opencode|cursor, --model and --effort checked against the live model catalog; caller becomes parent; await is bounded (default 30s, max 300s).

src-session-cli.title: Podium apps/cli/src/session-cli.ts
src-session-cli.finding: Session CLI: send (--wake queues and resumes a parked session), continue (errored phase only), status (no transcript text), read, recap, ask, title, handoff to another machine (target must be online; harness must support it), stop (frees worktree, keeps branch).

src-mcp.title: Podium apps/server/src/mcp-route.ts
src-mcp.finding: Server exposes a minimal stateless tools-only MCP endpoint over HTTP JSON-RPC (initialize, tools/list, tools/call), bearer-token gated, intended for loopback use by harness agents.

src-issue-mcp.title: Podium apps/server/src/issue-mcp.ts
src-issue-mcp.finding: Issue MCP tools are generated from the shared ISSUE_COMMANDS registry as issue_<command> tools, so CLI and MCP operate on the same issue commands.

src-automation-decide.title: Podium automations/decide.ts
src-automation-decide.finding: Pure scheduler decision: occurrences more than one hour late are recorded missed and not backfilled; an automation whose previous session is still live is skipped as overlap; otherwise a session is spawned.

src-automation-scheduler.title: Podium automations/scheduler.ts
src-automation-scheduler.finding: Server-owned scheduler ticks every 30 seconds after a 20 second boot delay, single-flight, inert until an enabled automation exists; schedule kinds are cron and once (model automation.ts line 48).

src-approvals.title: Podium approvals/service.ts
src-approvals.finding: Approval broker: agents request management operations through the relay, the operator approves or denies, the owning daemon executes, every step is appended to the issue activity log and the outcome is mailed to the agent; pending approvals are durable rows with no timeout.

src-approval-cli.title: Podium apps/cli/src/approval-cli.ts
src-approval-cli.finding: Inside a managed session, management commands block up to 10 minutes for an operator decision; denied or failed requests exit nonzero; on timeout the request stays valid and the outcome arrives as issue mail.

src-authz.title: Podium packages/model/src/authz/issue-authz.ts
src-authz.finding: Issue authorization policy defines viewer, worker and admin roles mapped to read, write and manage actions with closed scope kinds (all, none, subtree, owned, self). Source comment at lines 58-62 says the current scope is all and subtree is the reserved per-issue extension. The operator is unconstrained and agents carry a constrained capability. Commands carry actor and on-behalf-of fields.

src-auto-continue.title: Podium apps/server/src/auto-continue.ts
src-auto-continue.finding: When a global master switch is on, sessions in a retryable errored phase receive continue on escalating backoff from 10 seconds to a 5 minute cap until they recover.

src-prefs.title: Podium packages/model/src/settings/preferences.ts
src-prefs.finding: Settings defaults: auto-continue off; worktree GC mode propose after 14 days; git workflow mergeStyle ff-only | pr | ask (default ff-only) and autoRebaseBeforeMerge default true.

src-repo-op.title: Podium apps/daemon/src/repo-op.ts
src-repo-op.finding: Daemon repo operations include a guarded gh pr create --base <parent> --head <branch> --fill, used by the issue action pr.

src-usage-view.title: Podium apps/web/src/features/usage/UsageView.tsx
src-usage-view.finding: Usage and analytics sheet shows what the machine agents spent at hour resolution over seven days, leading with list-price cost, with a quota ledger and per-task costs.

src-quota-cli.title: Podium apps/cli/src/quota-cli.ts
src-quota-cli.finding: podium quota shows current plan usage limits per harness for each online daemon (account, plan, percent used, reset time), cached up to two minutes; it reports usage and is not a spend limit.

src-notify.title: Podium notify/service.ts
src-notify.finding: Notification service pushes attention notices through web clients, ntfy topics and Telegram chats; gated by the notifications feature flag (edge visibility, default off).

src-pointer.title: Podium packages/harness/src/issue-system-pointer.ts
src-pointer.finding: Podium injects an always-on issue-tracker pointer into the interactive Claude Code system prompt at main d3d67cf. Hook-delivered prime context (prime-injector) re-primes after compaction; the v0.1.0 injector handles Claude hook events, and delivery to other harnesses was not established.

src-linear.title: Podium superagent/tools.ts
src-linear.finding: When a Linear API key is configured the in-product superagent gets linear_search, linear_create and linear_move tools that call the Linear GraphQL API; these are assistant tool calls, not a sync of Podium issues.

src-harness-enum.title: Podium packages/model/src/entities/agent.ts
src-harness-enum.finding: Harness agent kinds: claude-code, codex, grok, opencode, cursor, pi.

src-host-metrics.title: Podium apps/daemon/src/host-metrics.ts
src-host-metrics.locator: parseMeminfo; host load, memory and disk wires
src-host-metrics.finding: Daemon samples host memory, load and disk; the web client shows host load and memory panels and hibernation policy reacts to pressure.

src-agent-guide.title: Podium docs/agents/podium-issues.md
src-agent-guide.locator: The loop; Repairing issue structure; Issue artifacts; Offering next actions
src-agent-guide.finding: Agent guide in the repository: issue prime, ready, comment checkpoints, discovered-from and blocks dependencies, supersede/duplicate/reparent repairs, artifact snapshots stored server-side, offers as clickable next actions and the merge-lock landing policy. Agents may write their own subtree; an edit outside it is refused once and needs --outside-scope; delete and restore are operator-only. A Podium-Issue commit trailer appears only as an example in a table about writing issue references.

v010-session-authz.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/sessions/session-authz.ts at v0.1.0
v010-session-authz.finding: At the v0.1.0 tag a relayed agent session presents a worker capability scoped to the subtree of its own issue (explicit attachment, else the issue owning its working directory), or scope none when it has no issue. The same code exists at main d3d67cf (line 268). The operator and web carry an unconstrained capability.

v010-issue-gate.title: Podium apps/server/src/issue-authz.ts at v0.1.0
v010-issue-gate.finding: The server gate refuses a constrained capability writing an existing issue outside its subtree with PRECONDITION_FAILED ("outside your subtree; re-run with --outside-scope to confirm") and lets an overrideScope flag from the CLI pass; a role without the action is forbidden. A scope of all returns without a subtree check.

v010-authz-model.title: Podium packages/model/src/authz/issue-authz.ts at v0.1.0
v010-authz-model.finding: The comment that says scope is all today describes the default capability model; authorize implements subtree, none, owned and self branches (subtree: write outside rootId needs override). Identical in substance at main d3d67cf.

v010-features.title: Podium packages/protocol/src/features.ts at v0.1.0
v010-features.finding: At v0.1.0 the specs feature is registered with edge visibility and described as showing living specs and giving agents spec-aware instructions and CLI guidance; edge features default off.

v010-cli.title: Podium apps/cli/src/cli.ts at v0.1.0
v010-cli.finding: At v0.1.0 the CLI parses and dispatches podium spec with no feature check; only the top-level help line for spec is shown when the specs feature is enabled. Same structure at main d3d67cf.

v010-spec-pointer-gate.title: Podium apps/server/src/relay.ts at v0.1.0
v010-spec-pointer-gate.finding: At v0.1.0 the issue pointer is registered unconditionally while the spec pointer is injected only when the specs feature is enabled, so agents are told about the spec CLI only with the flag on.

v010-prime-injector.title: Podium apps/daemon/src/prime-injector.ts at v0.1.0
v010-prime-injector.finding: At v0.1.0 prime context is injected once per session start and re-armed after PreCompact so it is re-injected after compaction. Present at main d3d67cf as well.

v010-attach-session.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/issues/registry.ts at v0.1.0
v010-attach-session.finding: At v0.1.0 attachSession is deliberately not scope-gated (no target): re-homing the calling session onto another issue needs no --outside-scope. A non-all (agent) caller cannot attach a session to, or file a sub-issue under, a proposed issue (assertNotProposedForAgent; spec SP-6144). Same code at main d3d67cf, lines 717-745.

v010-attach-anchor.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/issues/service/attention.ts at v0.1.0
v010-attach-anchor.locator: attachSession 114-190 (anchorId 153; startNow false 170; parentId anchorId 173; audience human 179); main d3d67cf attention.ts 161, 181, 187 and registry.ts attachSession 721-729
v010-attach-anchor.finding: attachSession with newSubissue and no targetId uses the session current issue as the anchor (prevId ?? targetId) and creates the child through crud().create with parentId set to that anchor, startNow false and audience human, then re-homes the session onto it. The registry-level assertNotProposedForAgent check runs only when input.targetId is present, so the anchor is not checked against the proposed stage on this path. The create command handler (registry.ts v0.1.0 523-566) does not use this path. Same logic at main d3d67cf.

podium:PLAN-08.answer: The spec CLI and service (living specs under pspec with stable SP IDs) are in the v0.1.0 source and at main 652072f. The podium spec command itself is dispatched, and the server specs service has no flag check, so direct CLI use does not need the flag. This agrees with the docs, which call specs not baseline rather than blocked. Not run end to end.
