changelog.finding: Changelog at main lists an Unreleased section (machine rekey, automatic pre-migration database snapshot, Podium Connect on by default for servers with a public URL, wire version bump) and 0.1.1-edge.4 additions (release pipeline, signed updates, desktop webview served from connected server, native iOS round for mobile).

security-md.title: Podium SECURITY.md
security-md.finding: Vulnerabilities are reported privately via GitHub Security Advisories or email; acknowledgement within 7 days is stated; only the latest release and main get fixes; server is designed for loopback or an authenticated proxy; agent sessions execute real shell commands.

telemetry-doc.title: Podium telemetry contract
telemetry-doc.locator: Short version; What is sent; Where it goes; Who sends
telemetry-doc.finding: Telemetry is off by default, asked once at the end of podium setup, sends at most one daily usage report and rate-limited crash reports with fixed-schema fields, never paths, prompts, transcripts or code, drops IP at a Podium-operated relay, forwards to PostHog Cloud, and is disabled by DO_NOT_TRACK=1 or PODIUM_TELEMETRY=off.

doc-home.title: Run coding agents with Podium
doc-home.finding: Docs home: Podium runs native Claude Code, Codex, Grok, OpenCode, Cursor and Pi processes on machines you control; supported core is a local or self-hosted control system; packaged desktop supports macOS, headless bundles Linux x86_64/ARM64, Linux AppImage preview, Windows experimental and not in the default release matrix; built first for one operator supervising several agents.

doc-availability.title: Check feature availability
doc-availability.locator: Supported core; Conditional; Preview; Experimental; Hosted
doc-availability.finding: Separates supported core (macOS desktop incl. Intel, headless Linux, issues, dependencies, worktrees, artifacts, offers, mail, multi-machine pairing, file browsing, stable/edge channels, opt-in telemetry) from conditional paths, preview clients (Linux AppImage; Windows experimental; native iPhone not confirmed; /mobile web build unsupported), experimental features (cloud runtimes, workflows, specs, automations, notifications, queues, shipping, handoff) and unconfirmed hosted behavior (billing, metering, retention controls not implemented).

doc-install.title: Install and set up Podium
doc-install.locator: Choose a supported deployment; First-run setup; Remote access
doc-install.finding: Install paths: macOS desktop (Apple silicon and Intel), headless Linux x86_64/ARM64 via signed installer, Linux AppImage preview, Windows experimental, hosted Podium unconfirmed. Setup registers a Git repository, detects installed harnesses and login state, offers a telemetry choice, and supports Tailscale, Cloudflare quick tunnel or reverse proxy access.

doc-quickstart.title: Complete your first issue
doc-quickstart.finding: Documented first-task loop: podium status, issue create, issue start --agent (creates branch and worktree), follow with issue show and session status, review evidence, close or merge. Requires a configured instance, a registered Git repository and one installed, authenticated harness.

doc-how.title: Understand how Podium runs agents
doc-how.finding: Server owns issues, sessions, artifacts; a daemon on each machine launches harnesses in real pseudo-terminals and connects outward; clients attach to live terminals and disconnecting does not end the session; mobile clients expose attention, issues, sessions and terminals but native iPhone release is not confirmed.

doc-agents.title: Understand issues, sessions, agents, and harnesses
doc-agents.finding: Issues are durable work records separate from sessions; one issue can retain several sessions; stopping a process hibernates a resumable session keeping transcript and branch; harness capabilities differ by harness.

doc-workspaces.title: Understand repositories, worktrees, and machines
doc-workspaces.finding: Repositories are registered per machine and can be cloned from a cloneable origin into ~/podium-repos; issues own a branch and linked worktree; Podium will not resolve branch conflicts; workspace fetch exposes another agent files read-only across machines.

doc-create.title: Create and track issue work
doc-create.locator: Create; Start or claim; State and todos; Dependencies; Close
doc-create.finding: CLI for creating, starting, planning, claiming, stating, todo checkpoints, blocking and discovered-from dependencies, spinoff attach and closing; agent-filed top-level issues land in proposed; operator-created issues start in backlog.

doc-delegate.title: Delegate work to other agents
doc-delegate.locator: Work shapes; spawn; child issue; mail; leases
doc-delegate.finding: Delegation shapes: another session on the same issue, child issue with its own worktree, or discovered-from top-level issue; podium agent spawn/status/await; durable mail with optional expected response; advisory lock leases. States Podium does not serialize agents editing one worktree.

doc-review.title: Review and accept agent work
doc-review.locator: Move to review; Check; Offer; Accept
doc-review.finding: Review path: issue artifacts, stage review, diff and checks, podium offer buttons, merge under merge-lock, issue action merge closes the issue; feedback action keeps it open.

doc-supervise.title: Supervise a running agent session
doc-supervise.locator: Status; Read; Send; Stop; Attention states
doc-supervise.finding: Supervision commands: session status/read/recap/send (--wake)/continue/stop; stop refuses a dirty managed worktree unless forced; attention states (needs input, idle, working, retryable error, permission request).

doc-machine.title: Add a remote machine
doc-machine.finding: Settings, Machines, Add machine creates a single-use hour-long pairing install command for a Linux host; verify with machine list/show/reprobe; place issues with issue start --machine; portable session handoff is not baseline stable.

doc-cli.title: Use the Podium CLI
doc-cli.finding: Stable command groups: lifecycle (setup, status, stop, logs, update, channel), work (issue, session, agent, mail, offer, worktree, workspace, lock, merge-lock), machines and access (machine, auth, quota, telemetry). Workflow, spec, automation, notification, shipping and handoff commands are behind default-off flags and not baseline.

doc-config.title: Configure a Podium installation
doc-config.locator: State root; Operator keys; Environment overrides
doc-config.finding: State (SQLite database, uploads, transcripts, artifacts, logs, daemon identity) lives in ~/.podium; modes all-in-one/server/daemon/client/supervisor; telemetry keys off unless enabled; transcriptLake default on; unlisted PODIUM_* variables are not a public contract.

doc-lifecycle.title: Reference issue and session states
doc-lifecycle.locator: Issue stages; Session states; Dependency meanings
doc-lifecycle.finding: Issue stages proposed/backlog/planning/in_progress/review/shipping/done; session states working/idle/needs input/permission needed/retryable error/hibernated; close reasons; defined dependency types blocks, related, parent-child, discovered-from, tracks, supersedes, caused-by, validates.

doc-privacy.title: Protect Podium data and credentials
doc-privacy.locator: Pairing; Stored data; Review agent actions; Telemetry; Website analytics
doc-privacy.finding: Daemons connect outward; pairing codes expire in one hour and can copy Claude Code and Codex credentials only when enabled; artifacts are immutable server copies; lifecycle commands and automation requests may need operator approval; harnesses run with host account permissions; telemetry opt-in; hosted app PostHog and website Google Analytics are separate paths.

doc-update.title: Update and back up Podium
doc-update.finding: Backups are a stopped copy of the state root; Podium writes a database-only migration snapshot (three retained) before migrations; updater verifies release signatures; an epoch-safe restore exists in the build but is not wired to a shipped command.

doc-trouble.title: Troubleshoot Podium by layer
doc-trouble.locator: First checks; Issue cannot start; Diagnostics
doc-trouble.finding: Layered troubleshooting; an issue cannot start if blocked by an open dependency, machine offline, repository absent, harness not logged in, or worktree conflict; crash export command.

src-agent-cli.title: Podium apps/cli/src/agent-cli.ts
src-agent-cli.finding: podium agent spawn starts a full Podium session (real PTY, visible in the UI) on an issue with --harness claude-code|codex|grok|opencode|cursor, --model and --effort checked against the live model catalog; caller becomes parent; await is bounded (default 30s, max 300s).

src-session-cli.title: Podium apps/cli/src/session-cli.ts
src-session-cli.finding: Session CLI: send (--wake queues and resumes a parked session), continue (errored phase only), status (no transcript text), read, recap, ask, title, handoff to another machine (target must be online; harness must support it), stop (frees worktree, keeps branch).

src-mcp.title: Podium apps/server/src/mcp-route.ts
src-mcp.finding: Server exposes a minimal stateless tools-only MCP endpoint over HTTP JSON-RPC (initialize, tools/list, tools/call), bearer-token gated, intended for loopback use by harness agents.

src-issue-mcp.title: Podium apps/server/src/issue-mcp.ts
src-issue-mcp.finding: Issue MCP tools are generated from the shared ISSUE_COMMANDS registry as issue_<command> tools, so CLI and MCP operate on the same issue commands.

src-automation-decide.title: Podium automations/decide.ts
src-automation-decide.finding: Pure scheduler decision: occurrences more than one hour late are recorded missed and not backfilled; an automation whose previous session is still live is skipped as overlap; otherwise a session is spawned.

src-automation-scheduler.title: Podium automations/scheduler.ts
src-automation-scheduler.finding: Server-owned scheduler ticks every 30 seconds after a 20 second boot delay, single-flight, inert until an enabled automation exists; schedule kinds are cron and once (model automation.ts line 48).

src-approvals.title: Podium approvals/service.ts
src-approvals.finding: Approval broker: agents request management operations through the relay, the operator approves or denies, the owning daemon executes, every step is appended to the issue activity log and the outcome is mailed to the agent; pending approvals are durable rows with no timeout.

src-approval-cli.title: Podium apps/cli/src/approval-cli.ts
src-approval-cli.finding: Inside a managed session, management commands block up to 10 minutes for an operator decision; denied or failed requests exit nonzero; on timeout the request stays valid and the outcome arrives as issue mail.

src-authz.title: Podium packages/model/src/authz/issue-authz.ts
src-authz.finding: Issue authorization policy defines viewer, worker and admin roles mapped to read, write and manage actions with closed scope kinds (all, none, subtree, owned, self). Source comment at lines 58-62 says the current scope is all and subtree is the reserved per-issue extension. The operator is unconstrained and agents carry a constrained capability. Commands carry actor and on-behalf-of fields.

src-auto-continue.title: Podium apps/server/src/auto-continue.ts
src-auto-continue.finding: When a global master switch is on, sessions in a retryable errored phase receive continue on escalating backoff from 10 seconds to a 5 minute cap until they recover.

src-prefs.title: Podium packages/model/src/settings/preferences.ts
src-prefs.finding: Settings defaults: auto-continue off; worktree GC mode propose after 14 days; git workflow mergeStyle ff-only | pr | ask (default ff-only) and autoRebaseBeforeMerge default true.

src-repo-op.title: Podium apps/daemon/src/repo-op.ts
src-repo-op.finding: Daemon repo operations include a guarded gh pr create --base <parent> --head <branch> --fill, used by the issue action pr.

src-usage-view.title: Podium apps/web/src/features/usage/UsageView.tsx
src-usage-view.finding: Usage and analytics sheet shows what the machine agents spent at hour resolution over seven days, leading with list-price cost, with a quota ledger and per-task costs.

src-quota-cli.title: Podium apps/cli/src/quota-cli.ts
src-quota-cli.finding: podium quota shows current plan usage limits per harness for each online daemon (account, plan, percent used, reset time), cached up to two minutes; it reports usage and is not a spend limit.

src-notify.title: Podium notify/service.ts
src-notify.locator: NotifyService; attentionNoticeName uses machinePathBasename; ntfy/Telegram pushers
src-notify.finding: Notification service pushes attention notices through web clients, ntfy topics and Telegram chats; gated by the notifications feature flag (edge visibility, default off).

src-pointer.title: Podium packages/harness/src/issue-system-pointer.ts
src-pointer.locator: ISSUE_SYSTEM_POINTER 10 onward; comment describes all harnesses through session instructions
src-pointer.finding: The always-on issue-system pointer is delivered through the podium:issues session instruction. It now tells agents to move finished work to review and offer Close, and to close their own issue only on user instruction. Server working-session close checks are separately implemented and can be overridden with confirmInterrupt.

src-linear.title: Podium superagent/tools.ts
src-linear.locator: linear tools in buildSuperagentTools; machinePathsEqual used for spawned-session lookup
src-linear.finding: When a Linear API key is configured the in-product superagent gets linear_search, linear_create and linear_move tools that call the Linear GraphQL API; these are assistant tool calls, not a sync of Podium issues.

src-harness-enum.title: Podium packages/model/src/entities/agent.ts
src-harness-enum.finding: Harness agent kinds: claude-code, codex, grok, opencode, cursor, pi.

src-host-metrics.title: Podium apps/daemon/src/host-metrics.ts
src-host-metrics.locator: parseMeminfo; host load, memory and disk wires
src-host-metrics.finding: Daemon samples host memory, load and disk; the web client shows host load and memory panels and hibernation policy reacts to pressure.

src-agent-guide.title: Podium docs/agents/podium-issues.md
src-agent-guide.locator: The loop step 7; scope and attach guidance; Issue artifacts; Offering next actions
src-agent-guide.finding: The agent guide retains subtree write scope, explicit file ownership, issue artifacts and offers. Step 7 now says to move to review, offer Close and close only on user instruction; an agent close while sessions work needs --confirm-interrupt.

v010-session-authz.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/sessions/session-authz.ts at v0.1.0
v010-session-authz.finding: At the v0.1.0 tag a relayed agent session presents a worker capability scoped to the subtree of its own issue (explicit attachment, else the issue owning its working directory), or scope none when it has no issue. The same code exists at main d3d67cf (line 268). The operator and web carry an unconstrained capability.

v010-issue-gate.title: Podium apps/server/src/issue-authz.ts at v0.1.0
v010-issue-gate.finding: The server gate refuses a constrained capability writing an existing issue outside its subtree with PRECONDITION_FAILED ("outside your subtree; re-run with --outside-scope to confirm") and lets an overrideScope flag from the CLI pass; a role without the action is forbidden. A scope of all returns without a subtree check.

v010-authz-model.title: Podium packages/model/src/authz/issue-authz.ts at v0.1.0
v010-authz-model.finding: The comment that says scope is all today describes the default capability model; authorize implements subtree, none, owned and self branches (subtree: write outside rootId needs override). Identical in substance at main d3d67cf.

v010-features.title: Podium packages/protocol/src/features.ts at v0.1.0
v010-features.finding: At v0.1.0 the specs feature is registered with edge visibility and described as showing living specs and giving agents spec-aware instructions and CLI guidance; edge features default off.

v010-cli.title: Podium apps/cli/src/cli.ts at v0.1.0
v010-cli.finding: At v0.1.0 the CLI parses and dispatches podium spec with no feature check; only the top-level help line for spec is shown when the specs feature is enabled. Same structure at main d3d67cf.

v010-spec-pointer-gate.title: Podium apps/server/src/relay.ts at v0.1.0
v010-spec-pointer-gate.finding: At v0.1.0 the issue pointer is registered unconditionally while the spec pointer is injected only when the specs feature is enabled, so agents are told about the spec CLI only with the flag on.

v010-prime-injector.title: Podium apps/daemon/src/prime-injector.ts at v0.1.0
v010-prime-injector.finding: At v0.1.0 prime context is injected once per session start and re-armed after PreCompact so it is re-injected after compaction. Present at main d3d67cf as well.

v010-attach-session.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/issues/registry.ts at v0.1.0
v010-attach-session.finding: At v0.1.0 attachSession is deliberately not scope-gated (no target): re-homing the calling session onto another issue needs no --outside-scope. A non-all (agent) caller cannot attach a session to, or file a sub-issue under, a proposed issue (assertNotProposedForAgent; spec SP-6144). Same code at main d3d67cf, lines 717-745.

v010-attach-anchor.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/issues/service/attention.ts at v0.1.0
v010-attach-anchor.locator: attachSession 114-190 (anchorId 153; startNow false 170; parentId anchorId 173; audience human 179); main d3d67cf attention.ts 161, 181, 187 and registry.ts attachSession 721-729
v010-attach-anchor.finding: attachSession with newSubissue and no targetId uses the session current issue as the anchor (prevId ?? targetId) and creates the child through crud().create with parentId set to that anchor, startNow false and audience human, then re-homes the session onto it. The registry-level assertNotProposedForAgent check runs only when input.targetId is present, so the anchor is not checked against the proposed stage on this path. The create command handler (registry.ts v0.1.0 523-566) does not use this path. Same logic at main d3d67cf.

oct9-windows.title: Podium packages/pty/vendor/podium-host/src/windows.rs
oct9-windows.locator: ConPTY host; named-pipe client authentication; process launch and signal handling
oct9-windows.finding: Current main includes a Windows ConPTY host and authenticated named-pipe transport. This establishes implementation only; the public download page still says Windows Coming soon.

oct9-start.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/sessions/session-start.ts
oct9-start.finding: Session start chooses explicit input.issueId, otherwise soleOwnerForCwd(input.cwd), and stores the chosen issue on the spawned session. This derivation has no Proposed-stage check.

oct9-cwd.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/issues/access-index.ts
oct9-cwd.finding: Cwd binding chooses the unique deepest non-deleted, non-archived issue worktree, excluding registered repository roots. It does not filter stage. A Proposed issue needs an existing recorded qualifying worktree for this route.

oct9-meta.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/sessions/session-meta-ops.ts
oct9-meta.finding: The explicit session issue ID is persisted without a Proposed-stage check; getSessionIssueId returns only explicit attachment, not cwd-derived capability scope.

oct9-attach.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/issues/service/attention.ts
oct9-attach.locator: attachSession 112-244, especially anchorId 161, create 178-199 and setSessionIssueId 220
oct9-attach.finding: With newSubissue and no targetId, attachSession uses the explicit current session issue as parent, calls CRUD create directly with startNow false and audience human, then attaches the existing session. A real parent requires confirmRehome; other active sessions can trigger the coordinator-replacement guard. No Proposed-stage check appears in this path.

oct9-crud.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/issues/service/crud.ts
oct9-crud.locator: create, stage default 975; audience 1016; parent linkage after persistence
oct9-crud.finding: CRUD create defaults stage to backlog and uses the provided audience. attachSession calls this layer directly, bypassing the registry create handler that keeps ordinary children of Proposed issues internal and unstarted.

oct9-authz.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/sessions/session-authz.ts
oct9-authz.finding: A known relayed session gets worker scope for its explicit issue subtree, falling back to issueForCwd, or none. The legacy model comment saying current scope is all is not the active capability minting behavior.

oct9-orchestrator.title: Podium apps/server/src/application/issue-attach-orchestrator.ts
oct9-orchestrator.finding: The authenticated attach orchestrator carries the principal through a transaction into attention.attachSession; it adds no Proposed-stage check.

oct9-boundary.title: Podium packages/harness/src/driver/families/boundary-hook.ts
oct9-boundary.finding: Shared Claude/Codex hook codec maps SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit and PreCompact to driver boundary context. SessionStart with source compact rearms before priming. Codex does not use PreCompact for additionalContext. Source inspected, not observed in this pass.

oct9-claude.title: Podium packages/harness/src/driver/families/claude-sdk/protocol.ts
oct9-claude.locator: initializePayload 204 onward; answerBoundaryHook; hook_callback; turn deadline near 1046
oct9-claude.finding: Claude stream engine receives appended instructions and in-band boundary callbacks. The turn deadline is armed only when timeoutMs is supplied; no default ten-minute timer remains in this driver. An explicit timeout interrupts and is classified separately.

oct9-codex.title: Podium packages/harness/src/driver/families/codex/runtime.ts
oct9-codex.locator: createWithId; instructionsText(spec) passed to host launch
oct9-codex.finding: Codex server-family sessions pass session instructions to their host as developer instructions. This is current source, not a stable-release or all-harness memory guarantee.

oct9-grok.title: Podium packages/harness/src/driver/families/grok-acp/runtime.ts
oct9-grok.finding: Grok ACP sends instructions through _meta.rules. Comments describe upstream CLI measurement; this research pass inspected code and did not repeat that measurement.

oct9-opencode.title: Podium packages/harness/src/driver/families/opencode/runtime.ts
oct9-opencode.finding: OpenCode sends session instructions as the prompt system field. Adopted sessions have a separate context path; no blanket cross-harness takeover guarantee follows.

oct9-session.title: Podium apps/daemon/src/control/session.ts
oct9-session.finding: Current main carries Podium instructions and relay environment through terminal and engine launch. Terminal reattachment now goes through runtime.adopt and a registered handle. A surviving process is required; this is not proof of recovery from worker death.

oct9-config.title: Podium packages/runtime/src/config.ts
oct9-config.locator: transcriptLake schema 343-350, layered default 1842-1848, resolveTranscriptLake 2109 onward
oct9-config.finding: Transcript mirroring defaults on, with environment, file and Settings precedence. This corrects the earlier claim that the default had not been source-verified at main.

oct9-lake.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/memory/lake.ts
oct9-lake.finding: Server code mirrors daemon transcript bytes and indexes conversations. Conversation recall does not establish curated memory, repository-code search, or memory correction/deletion controls.

oct9-inbox.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/sessions/inbox.ts
oct9-inbox.finding: A controller-origin human chat defaults to steer; other senders default when-ready. The initial prompt remains when-ready. Durability alone does not prove that a harness has consumed the prompt.

oct9-terminal.title: Podium packages/harness/src/driver/families/terminal/runtime.ts
oct9-terminal.finding: A busy terminal with queuesBusyInput takes steer input into the native TUI queue. Undeclared harnesses downgrade to queue; compaction waits. Terminal adoption validates process identity and observation lease. No live steering or restart scenario was run.

oct9-headless.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/superagent/headless.ts
oct9-headless.finding: The one-shot headless server runner supplies timeoutMs, default 600000ms, to the daemon so its wait and enforced deadline agree. This is a source-level per-call budget, not a general operator token/spend limit.

oct9-turn.title: Podium packages/harness/src/driver/families/headless/turn.ts
oct9-turn.finding: Hosted headless turns enforce a supplied timeoutMs; absent timeoutMs does not arm a turn deadline. Other lifecycle, provider and explicit-call limits remain separate.

v010-start.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/sessions/session-start.ts
v010-start.finding: Public v0.1.0 start derives explicit issueId or soleOwnerForCwd and persists the attachment without a Proposed-stage filter.

v010-cwd.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/issues/service/reads.ts
v010-cwd.finding: Public v0.1.0 cwd binding filters deleted, archived, repository-root and ambiguous worktrees, but not Proposed stage.

v010-meta.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/sessions/session-meta-ops.ts
v010-meta.finding: Public v0.1.0 explicit attachment has no stage filter; attachSession reads the explicit session issue rather than the capability cwd fallback.

v010-crud.title: Podium apps/server/src/modules/issues/service/crud.ts
v010-crud.finding: Public v0.1.0 CRUD create defaults to backlog and accepts audience human. The attach child is unstarted but has a live session attached; startNow false alone does not make it inert.

oct9-public-tag.title: Public v0.1.0 tag identity
oct9-public-tag.finding: Public annotated tag b14874fb4a0391985a461ed9fe310d66ed5a5668 peels to commit 241dd542e1494c68080d5fd2ef441d7c2e195b12. The local tag resolves differently and was not used to establish public-release behavior.

oct9-roadmap.title: Public issue and roadmap scan
oct9-roadmap.finding: Seven open entries are six dependency PRs and one Windows file-durability PR. No feature roadmap or dated capability announcement was identified. Official /roadmap, /changelog and /docs/roadmap.md returned 404; CHANGELOG remains unchanged from the previous source pin.

oct9-pricing.title: Public pricing search
oct9-pricing.locator: HTTP response; home, download and feature availability docs
oct9-pricing.finding: Pricing route returned 404 on 2026-10-09 with the research User-Agent. No price table was found on the checked official pages. This is a bounded search result, not a claim that pricing cannot exist elsewhere.

oct9-doc-index.title: Published documentation index
oct9-doc-index.locator: 20 page links, including local development and deployment
oct9-doc-index.finding: Documentation index and all 20 linked Markdown pages were retrieved. Product docs retain the supported-core/default-off/hosted-unconfirmed distinctions; developer pages describe docs tooling, not product features.

oct9-busy-claude-code.title: Podium claude-code terminal manifest
oct9-busy-claude-code.finding: The claude-code terminal manifest declares queuesBusyInput true. Together with the terminal driver this enables immediate typing of human steer input into a running native queue. Native consumption and timing were not observed in this research pass.

oct9-busy-codex.title: Podium codex terminal manifest
oct9-busy-codex.finding: The codex terminal manifest declares queuesBusyInput true. Together with the terminal driver this enables immediate typing of human steer input into a running native queue. Native consumption and timing were not observed in this research pass.

oct9-busy-grok.title: Podium grok terminal manifest
oct9-busy-grok.finding: The grok terminal manifest declares queuesBusyInput true. Together with the terminal driver this enables immediate typing of human steer input into a running native queue. Native consumption and timing were not observed in this research pass.

oct9-busy-opencode.title: Podium opencode terminal manifest
oct9-busy-opencode.finding: The opencode terminal manifest declares queuesBusyInput true. Together with the terminal driver this enables immediate typing of human steer input into a running native queue. Native consumption and timing were not observed in this research pass.

changes.summary: Independent review accepted 48 public candidates after checking the factual delta, unchanged-source mappings, public stable identity, Proposed attachment trace, driver instructions/steering/deadlines and backup documentation. Named harness and execution scopes are explicit, stale line-number prose was corrected, and three unsupported-by-evidence unknown rows remain internal. No runtime test or stable parity for main-only changes is implied.

Recorded the flight deck, Pi, cost per task, experimental Windows and Linux desktop, and the memory benchmark as a vendor claim. A Linux x86_64 AppImage is preview/experimental and Windows is not offered. A native iPhone app is described as private beta, not publicly distributed. podium:PLAN-07.answer: CLI and MCP address the same canonical issue records for reads, creation, edits, claims, state, dependencies and artifacts. Relayed agents have worker capability scoped to their issue subtree, with --outside-scope confirmation for other existing issues. attachSession is not subtree-gated, but direct rehoming from a real issue is refused and an agent attach naming a Proposed target is refused. That does not make every Proposed subtree inert: operator attachment or spawn-time cwd binding can leave a session explicitly attached to a Proposed issue; newSubissue without targetId then bypasses the proposed-parent guard, creates a human-audience backlog child with startNow false, and attaches the existing session. This path exists in both public v0.1.0 and current main source. It was not exercised live. Concurrent-edit handling remains unknown.
podium:PLAN-07.scopeVersion: Public docs retrieved 2026-10-09; public main 652072f70f9decf1fe161b04cefee218cca5aed0 (committed 2026-10-08 UTC, 2026-10-09 Europe/Berlin); stable v0.1.0 public commit 241dd542e1494c68080d5fd2ef441d7c2e195b12, released 2026-08-21. permissions.answer: Viewer, worker and admin issue roles exist. A relayed agent receives worker/subtree scope, or none without an issue; --outside-scope confirms other existing-issue writes. Delete/restore are operator-only. attachSession is not subtree-gated, but real-issue direct rehoming is refused. Its Proposed guard only checks a supplied targetId for constrained callers. Operator attachment is allowed from a draft/unbound session; spawn can persist a Proposed issue attachment through a qualifying cwd because soleOwnerForCwd has no stage filter. Given that explicit attachment, newSubissue with no targetId and confirmRehome creates a human-facing backlog child and attaches the session, bypassing registry create protections. A qualifying cwd must have an existing recorded unique deepest non-archived worktree outside registered repository roots; an ordinary new proposal has no such worktree. Current main and public v0.1.0 have this source path, not a verified live exploit. Current main also has an overridable working-session close guard.

podium:PLAN-08.answer: The spec CLI and service (living specs under pspec with stable SP IDs) are in the v0.1.0 source and at main 652072f. Specs is an experimental, default-off (edge) feature: the flag controls the Specs UI, the spec line in CLI help and whether agents are told about the spec CLI (the spec system pointer is injected only when it is on). podium:PLAN-03.answer: Podium supports persistent parent and child issues, phases and typed dependency links, including reparenting an existing issue without replacing its identity. Since 0.3.0 issue types are task, phase and decision: epic and other kinds are retired, and any issue with children acts as a parent. Dependency types are fixed to blocked-by, related, discovered-from, supersedes and duplicates. Cycles are refused and docs list an open blocker as a reason an issue cannot start. No mandatory workflow preset applies in the baseline.

epics.answer: Any issue can contain sub-issues; the epic issue type is retired, and the root of a tree acts as the mission. Phases group tasks.

blockers.answer: Typed blocked-by dependencies are persisted separately from containment. The fixed types are blocked-by, related, discovered-from, supersedes and duplicates; blocks is no longer accepted. Phases take no blocked-by edge.

state_propagation.answer: The deck rolls state words and counts up from leaf tasks as a derived view. Source comments say a phase never closes by itself. Whether closing children changes a parent stage is otherwise not established.

podium:PLAN-04.answer: v0.3.0 routes Podium issue instructions and relay environment through terminal and engine session launch. Claude stream sessions use appended instructions and boundary callbacks; Codex server sessions use developer instructions, Grok ACP uses rules, and OpenCode uses the prompt system field. Claude and Codex boundary hooks can re-prime after compaction. Transcript mirroring is on by default; full-text indexing needs the command-palette flag, which defaults off. Agent profiles can carry markdown instructions. Curated memory, skills and memory correction or deletion controls remain unestablished. No instruction-delivery or compaction scenario was run.

podium:PLAN-05.answer: Not established. Podium mirrors daemon transcripts by default, keeps a full-text index only when the command-palette flag is on, and stores session attachments. No repository code search, architecture awareness or API retrieval feature was found.

idea_parking.answer: Operator issues start in backlog and agent proposals in proposed, shown on the deck; creation does not require starting an agent.

metadata.answer: Title, description, brief, acceptance, priority, labels, assignee, stage, type, parent, dependencies and agent profile. Task colors were dropped in 0.3.0.

podium:PLAN-07.answer: CLI and MCP address the same canonical issue records for reads, creation, edits, claims, state, dependencies and artifacts. Relayed agents have worker capability scoped to their issue subtree, with --outside-scope confirmation for other existing issues. attachSession is not subtree-gated, but direct rehoming from a real issue is refused and an agent attach naming a Proposed target is refused. That does not make every Proposed subtree inert: operator attachment or spawn-time cwd binding can leave a session attached to a Proposed issue; newSubissue without targetId then bypasses the proposed-parent guard, creates a human-audience backlog child and attaches the existing session. This path remains at v0.3.0 source and was not exercised live. Concurrent-edit handling remains unknown.
podium:PLAN-07.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. Docs that predate the release are noted where they differ. No product runtime scenario run.

permissions.answer: Viewer, worker and admin issue roles exist. A relayed agent receives worker/subtree scope, or none without an issue; --outside-scope confirms other existing-issue writes. Delete and restore are operator-only; only the user closes a decision issue. attachSession is not subtree-gated, but real-issue direct rehoming is refused. Its Proposed guard only checks a supplied targetId for constrained callers. Operator attachment is allowed from a draft session; spawn can persist a Proposed issue attachment through a qualifying cwd when mayJoinIssue passes, because soleOwnerForCwd has no stage filter. Given that attachment, newSubissue with no targetId and confirmRehome creates a human-audience backlog child and attaches the session, bypassing registry create protections. This is a source path, not a verified live exploit.

podium:PLAN-08.answer: The spec CLI and service (living specs under pspec with stable SP IDs) are in v0.3.0. Specs is an experimental, default-off feature listed on the edge channel: the flag controls the Specs UI, the spec line in CLI help and whether agents are told about the spec CLI. The podium spec command itself is dispatched, and the server specs service has no flag check, so direct CLI use does not need the flag. This agrees with the docs, which call specs not baseline rather than blocked. Not run end to end.

human_edits.answer: The Specs UI is behind the default-off edge specs flag; the spec files can be edited directly and through the CLI without it (source, not run).

agent_edits.answer: The CLI supports create, update, remove, search and read and its dispatch is not feature-gated; agents are given spec instructions only when the specs flag is on, so by default they are not prompted to use it. Source only.

review_integration.answer: When the specs flag is on, agent instructions require reading applicable specs and escalating contradictions; with it off (default) agents are not given that guidance. Automatic drift enforcement or a shipping gate is not established.

podium:COORD-01.answer: Docs and release notes describe many sessions running as independent terminals, one worktree per issue, and several paired machines under one server, with session and issue state visible on the flight deck, board and CLI. Agent-initiated spawns are limited to 10 per target issue per UTC day. Achieved concurrency is unmeasured.
podium:COORD-01.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. quotas.answer: Agent-initiated spawns are limited to 10 per target issue per UTC day, shared with mail-triggered spawns; human spawns are exempt. No overall concurrent-session limit was found.

status_visibility.answer: Session states and issue stages are documented. The 0.3.0 flight deck shows every task and its state with counts by Needs you, Active, Up next and Done; session status is also in the CLI.

podium:COORD-02.answer: Issues carry an assignee, claim sets assignee and in_progress, a coordinator session can be set per issue, sessions have seats, and work can be placed on a chosen machine or agent profile. claim has no exclusivity check of its own, locks are advisory leases and Podium does not serialize agents editing one worktree, so exclusive ownership is not enforced.
podium:COORD-02.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. claims.answer: claim sets assignee and moves the issue to in_progress. It is a plain update in source with no exclusivity check of its own; two claimants were not tested.

queues.answer: issue ready lists unblocked work and the deck shows Up next. The merge-queue flag and Queues panel were removed; a shipping queue remains behind the Shipping flag.

routing.answer: Issues can be placed on a named machine with issue start --machine, pick an agent profile with --profile, and a coordinator session can be designated. Seats route questions below a coordinator to issue mail.

podium:COORD-03.answer: Podium orchestrates delegation itself: podium agent spawn starts a full child session on an issue with a chosen harness, model, effort or agent profile, mail carries messages, and bounded await reports the child result. Children are real sessions shown as seats on the flight deck. Agent-initiated spawns take a daily budget per issue. A complete delegated task with retained child findings was not run.
podium:COORD-03.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. model_harness_effort.answer: spawn takes --harness, --model, --effort and --profile; profile candidates supply a setup when flags do not.

live_progress.answer: A child is a full session shown with a seat on the deck, and agent status reads its state.

podium:COORD-04.answer: The server owns a scheduler for cron and one-time automations that spawn agent sessions, skipping overlaps and not backfilling occurrences more than an hour late. The Automations UI is an edge-visibility feature that defaults off and docs list automations as non-baseline. Agents can subscribe to issue and session events.
podium:COORD-04.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. podium:COORD-05.answer: Chat and native CLI views share a session. v0.3.0 defaults human controller chat to steer and immediately types it into running Claude Code, Codex, Grok and OpenCode TUIs that declare native busy-input queuing; undeclared harnesses wait for a boundary, and compaction waits. Mail and automation keep when-ready delivery. Stop, resume, questions, decision issues and offers remain available. This is inspected implementation, not a cross-harness runtime parity result.
podium:COORD-05.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. steer.answer: Human controller chat defaults to steer. Terminal manifests declare queuesBusyInput for Claude Code, Codex, Grok and OpenCode; those paths type into the native busy TUI queue. Cursor and Pi do not declare it, other senders default when-ready, and compaction waits. Native harness consumption timing can differ. No in-run amendment scenario was run.

pending_decisions.answer: needs-human flags an issue with a question; decision issues count as Needs you and only the user closes them; offers present decisions; permission-needed is a session state.

podium:COORD-06.answer: Release 0.3.0 ships a flight deck showing a whole mission in one view: phases, every task and its state, who works on what, what is blocked and by what, and proposals. Done work stays visible. The CLI prints the same snapshot. The waterfall source is dormant and the Timeline view was deleted, so per-task timeline history is not shown. The shared 12-task UX scenario has not been run.
podium:COORD-06.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. Docs that predate the release are noted where they differ. No product runtime scenario run.

parent_child.answer: The deck renders phases, tasks and the sessions seated on each, from the server deck snapshot; sub-task counters roll up from leaf tasks.

dependencies.answer: Blocked tasks name what they wait on, and the Full view has a dependency layer. Blockers outside the deck are marked. A graph navigation test was not run.

attention.answer: Task and session state words include Needs you, Error, Working, Idle, Blocked and Not started, with counts and a Needs you filter.

history.answer: Done work stays visible on the deck, one click from its conversation. The waterfall view is dormant and the Timeline view was deleted, so no per-task timeline is shown.

podium:COORD-07.answer: A quick task can be an interactive session or an issue; an issue can grow into a mission by gaining children while keeping its identity; no mandatory workflow preset applies in the baseline. Per-agent harness, model and effort are chosen at spawn or through agent profiles, and the deck shows seats. The coordinator-with-two-reviewers scenario was not run.
podium:COORD-07.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. agent_configuration.answer: spawn accepts harness, model, effort and profile per child; profiles are edited by people, and agents can only pick one.

live_roles.answer: The deck lists each session with its seat, harness, model and effort, and a coordinator can be claimed per issue. Roles were not observed live.

podium:RUN-01.answer: Local desktop execution, a user-owned Linux VPS running the headless server, additional paired machines, and browser or phone reconnection are documented. The desktop app also runs locally on Linux and Windows in experimental builds. Managed Podium cloud availability is not confirmed.

local.answer: The macOS desktop app runs server, daemon and web UI locally. Experimental Linux and Windows desktop builds offer the same local choice.

podium:RUN-02.answer: Issue-backed work gets its own Git branch and linked worktree on the selected machine; a direct session can use the current checkout. Docs state harnesses run with the permissions of their host account and that Podium does not make generated commands safe. Container, VM and network isolation were not established.
podium:RUN-02.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. podium:RUN-03.answer: Closing a browser tab does not stop the agent process on a running Podium host. Idle sessions may hibernate under configurable policies; a stopped session keeps its transcript, branch and resume reference. Release 0.2.0 says a failed update rolls back and running sessions keep running through the upgrade; database rollback remains a manual restore. Terminal reattachment goes through the driver adopt contract with process-identity and observation-lease checks. Worker-crash and multi-day behavior were not tested.
podium:RUN-03.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. Docs that predate the release are noted where they differ. No product runtime scenario run.

service_restart.answer: Release 0.2.0 says sessions running during an upgrade keep running on the old terminal host until they end, with some limits, and that a failed update rolls back. The updater manages restart and health confirmation. No restart was run.

process_reconnect.answer: The daemon keeps the process available so a client can reattach to the same PTY. Terminal reattachment adopts the surviving process through the driver contract with process identity and lease checks; this was not run and does not establish recovery of a dead process.

manual_repair.answer: Database rollback means restoring podium.db.backup-vupdate-*. Docs add that an epoch-safe restore exists but is not wired to a shipped command, and a bare file copy can leave clients with stale state.

podium:RUN-04.answer: Only machine setup is documented: the installer installs missing runtime tools and pairs a host, and the state directory holds server-managed secrets. Dependency caching, services, ports and automatic repair for project environments were not found.
podium:RUN-04.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. Docs that predate the release are noted where they differ. No product runtime scenario run.

remote_setup.answer: The headless installer installs missing prerequisites through the system package manager and joins a machine with a pairing command; project dependency setup is not described.

podium:RUN-05.answer: Podium exposes retryable errors, optional auto-continue with backoff, bounded waits and provider quota. Claude stream and hosted headless drivers enforce a supplied turn deadline, with no deadline when timeoutMs is absent. The one-shot headless server runner supplies its budget, default ten minutes. Agent spawns have a daily per-issue budget. Operator-configurable task-wide turn, token and spend caps remain unestablished; quota display is not enforcement.
podium:RUN-05.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. Docs that predate the release are noted where they differ. No product runtime scenario run.

time_limits.answer: Driver APIs accept timeoutMs and enforce it per turn. The one-shot server runner supplies a default 600000ms budget; the Claude stream and hosted headless driver paths have no implicit deadline when timeoutMs is absent. This does not establish a general operator-configurable task time cap.

podium:RUN-06.answer: Podium offers local logs and crash export, structured session status, issue stats, a usage and analytics sheet with hourly list-price cost, per-task costs and host load panels. The 0.3.0 notes report a vendor benchmark of about 330 MB server memory against about 1.2 GB and 8 to 52 percent faster start; the method is published in the repository and was not reproduced here. Usage export and cross-reconnect consistency were not established.
podium:RUN-06.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. Docs that predate the release are noted where they differ. No product runtime scenario run.

task_stats.answer: Per-task token cost and issue counts through issue stats and the usage sheet.

performance_method.answer: Vendor bench published at docs/measurements/pod-6140-result.md: corpus sizes, load, runs and commits are stated. The headline is about 330 MB against about 1.2 GB server RSS and 8 to 52 percent faster boot. It is a vendor claim, not reproduced, and its live half is recorded as pending.

podium:RUN-07.answer: Since 0.2.0 Podium shows what each task costs, on the task header and the usage sheet, with per-session rows and descendant rollups. The 0.3.0 deck adds a mission cost chip. Figures are token estimates at public model list prices, not subscription invoices or provider bills.
podium:RUN-07.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. task_cost.answer: Task cost records in source; the 0.2.0 release shows them on the task header and usage sheet.

session_cost.answer: The task cost section lists each session with its own cost and harness, including finished sessions.

harness_aggregation.answer: Cost records carry the harnesses involved and each session row names its harness. A dedicated per-harness rollup across tasks was not established.

podium:RUN-08.answer: Podium reports host memory, load and disk, auto-hibernates idle sessions under pressure, and provides named advisory resource leases. The merge-queue panel was removed; a shipping queue remains behind the Shipping flag. Concurrency limits and bounded test queuing were not established.
podium:RUN-08.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. queues.answer: The merge-queue flag and Queues panel were removed. The Shipping feature keeps its own queue, edge-listed and default off.

Backend share handlers and a Members settings section with invites and admin or member roles exist; they do not establish a finished human collaboration workflow. Docs say small teams can share an instance but the interface prioritizes one operator.

permissions.answer: Backend share and unshare commands write permission grants, and Settings has member or admin instance roles. These do not establish a released human collaboration workflow.

podium:TEAM-02.answer: Source defines viewer, worker and admin roles for issue capabilities, and instance members are member or admin with invite and removal routes. Project roles, SSO and provisioning were not found, and hosted organizations are not confirmed in production.
podium:TEAM-02.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. organization_roles.answer: Instance members are member or admin; member routes require admin. Hosted organization roles are not confirmed in production.

task_roles.answer: Issue authorization defines viewer, worker and admin roles. capabilityForSession mints worker/subtree scope or none for relayed agents. This does not establish organization RBAC, SSO or a complete multiplayer workflow.

membership.answer: Settings Members offers invite links, optional email and member removal. Docs say hosted code includes accounts, organizations, invitations and device sessions, with production availability unconfirmed.

unauthorized_access.answer: Member routes answer 403 unless the actor is admin (source). A wider access test was not run.

revocation.answer: An admin can remove a member through the member routes. The effect on live sessions was not established.

podium:TEAM-03.answer: Agent-session management requests go through an operator approval broker with approve and deny; the privacy docs say lifecycle commands and automation requests may require operator approval. Harness permission prompts appear as a Permission needed state; credential copying during pairing is a per-grant opt-in. Command-level policy enforcement beyond the harness own modes was not established.
podium:TEAM-03.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. Docs that predate the release are noted where they differ. No product runtime scenario run.

podium:TEAM-04.answer: Issue activity is recorded in a durable event log readable by the events command, approval steps are appended to the issue activity feed, and comments and mail are retained. Export, immutability and retention guarantees were not established, so this is not an audit trail.
podium:TEAM-04.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. Docs that predate the release are noted where they differ. No product runtime scenario run.

podium:TEAM-05.answer: Review is a documented loop: issue stage review, diff and checks, artifacts, offers with merge or send-back buttons, and a Tray of review-ready work. Release 0.3.0 adds quoting text from a reply or review finding into the next message and a full-height reading view with an outline. The board has a key map with a help sheet. Guided-review quality and narrow-screen use were not measured.
podium:TEAM-05.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. Docs that predate the release are noted where they differ. No product runtime scenario run.

request_changes.answer: Offers carry a send-back action with typed feedback that revises the issue. Text from a reply or review finding can be quoted into the next message.

keyboard.answer: Board keys cover movement, selection, open, create and property menus with a ? help sheet; ⌘B toggles the deck. Keyboard-only review was not tested.

podium:TEAM-06.answer: The durable issue, session transcript, artifacts and mail persist for any later agent, and a live session can be handed to another machine in an edge feature. Colleague takeover by a second person was not established.
podium:TEAM-06.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. Docs that predate the release are noted where they differ. No product runtime scenario run.

podium:SHIP-01.answer: Artifact commands store immutable server-side copies of issue-linked files, including images, video, HTML and documents, which render in the issue sidebar and offers and stay readable after the worktree is gone. Each task has an artifacts page grouped into screens, documents and reports, with filters and search. Revision linking remains untested.
podium:SHIP-01.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. Docs that predate the release are noted where they differ. No product runtime scenario run.

recordings.answer: Artifacts recognize video as a kind and the site lists recordings on the artifact page. Capture itself is up to the agent.

test_outputs.answer: Files named as reports, reviews, audits, validation or results group under Reports. There is no dedicated test-output type.

reviewer_outputs.answer: Review and findings files group under Reports on the artifact page. There is no structured reviewer output.

gallery.answer: A task artifact page shows screens as a grid and documents and reports as a table, with filter chips and search. Offer cards show the first three.

podium:SHIP-02.answer: In the experimental Shipping path a configured validation profile runs before landing (default argv bun run test with a 10 minute timeout) and a failed validation holds the order. Lint, type, CI and spec conformance gates and independent review requirements were not found as product-enforced policy.
podium:SHIP-02.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. Docs that predate the release are noted where they differ. No product runtime scenario run.

podium:SHIP-03.answer: Issues own branches and worktrees, and issue actions rebase, open a pull request with gh (pr create --fill) and merge, subject to a merge-style setting (ff-only by default, with auto-rebase before merge). Podium does not resolve branch conflicts, and PR review comments and CI response were not established.
podium:SHIP-03.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. Docs that predate the release are noted where they differ. No product runtime scenario run.

pull_requests.answer: issue action pr runs gh pr create --base <parent> --head <branch> --fill and records the printed URL on the issue; mergeStyle can be pr; requires the GitHub CLI.

podium:SHIP-04.answer: The operator accepts work through offers and runs the merge action under a branch merge-lock; in the experimental Shipping path approval is frozen to an exact head and delivery lands on a local target branch by default. Release and deployment are not product features found in the sources.
podium:SHIP-04.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. Docs that predate the release are noted where they differ. No product runtime scenario run.

podium:SHIP-05.answer: Shipping orders record approved base and head SHAs, tested integration SHA, landed ref and validation result in a durable delivery receipt, and stale approvals hold the order. Shipping is experimental. The pr action records a PR URL on the issue. Build and deployment links and rollback were not found.
podium:SHIP-05.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. Docs that predate the release are noted where they differ. No product runtime scenario run.

pr_links.answer: issue action pr stores the PR URL on the issue; this is outside the Shipping receipt.

podium:SHIP-06.answer: The shipping service records revision-specific approval, configured validation and delivery receipts. The Shipping panel is an experimental edge toggle, off by default; the separate Queues panel was removed.
podium:SHIP-06.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. podium:OWN-02.answer: Local desktop and self-hosted installs run on user-controlled machines with a documented state directory. The docs describe stopped full-state backup and automatic pre-migration database-only snapshots retaining three copies. Those snapshots omit artifacts, transcripts, uploads, configuration and secrets; no portable structured export/import contract was established.
podium:OWN-02.scopeVersion: Public stable tag v0.3.0 (tag object ca1c848f97be633466d0abf161db46e9dd5659c5, commit ec6ff505f69aeb358eb744596e70e984996c2e42, released 2026-11-05); public docs and site retrieved 2026-11-06. vendor_dependencies.answer: Agents require each harness provider account; releases and updates come from GitHub with stable entrypoints on podium.do; usage telemetry is on by default and goes to a Podium relay unless turned off; Podium Connect can publish a public-URL server location to connect.podium.do. It is on by default once a public URL exists and one switch turns it off.

podium:OWN-03.answer: Docs state repositories and native harness credentials stay on machines you control and server state lives in a documented directory. Since 0.2.0 a daily usage report is on by default and can be turned off; crash reports stay opt-in. Both use a published fixed schema excluding paths, prompts, transcripts and code. Public docs still call telemetry opt-in; the v0.3.0 telemetry document and source are newer. Model-provider handling is the harness own. Hosted analytics and website analytics are separate paths.

telemetry_controls.answer: podium telemetry on/off/show/reset-id, Settings Privacy, DO_NOT_TRACK=1 and PODIUM_TELEMETRY=off.

consent_prompt.answer: The telemetry document at v0.3.0 says the choice is never asked during setup; it is a setting. Install docs still list a telemetry opt-in step.

podium:OWN-04.answer: No Podium price is published: podium.do/pricing returns 404 and the docs list billing as not implemented. The software is open source and free to download; model and compute costs are the user's own.

authentication.answer: Podium-owned MCP tools require a bearer token or x-podium-mcp-token; per-thread opaque tokens identify the assistant context. External provider-tool authentication remains the harness own.

permission_scope.answer: Podium tools use thread-scoped authority and start-capable operations fail closed for absent/unknown thread identity. This does not establish permission controls for user-configured external MCP servers.

scope.answer: Repository instructions/spec components are scoped to a repository. The experimental specs service restricts reads/writes to registered roots present on the server; maintained cross-harness memory scope remains unestablished.

provenance.answer: Experimental spec guidance says components codify explicit human decisions and links them through stable SP IDs/code references. It does not establish verified provenance for generated memory.

correction.answer: Experimental spec guidance tells agents to flag contradictory decisions and mark a resolved losing decision superseded instead of overwriting it. This is instruction, not a runtime enforcement result.

indexing.answer: The default-off command-palette option enables full-text indexing of conversation summaries and mirrored transcripts. This is internal-work history, not a code index.

api_retrieval.answer: The in-product assistant exposes search_conversations and search_all over internal history with bounded results; these are internal tools, not a documented public retrieval API.

citations.answer: Internal omni-search returns typed hits with identifiers, snippets and issue display references. No guarantee that final agent answers cite retrieved sources is established.

approvals.answer: Experimental living-spec instructions require explicit human decisions/context and flag contradictions for resolution. There is no inspected product-enforced approval gate for spec changes.

completion_conditions.answer: Experimental automations record dispatch outcomes rather than verifying the requested task outcome; a spawned session is not an accepted issue. Cron re-arms after each occurrence.

retries.answer: Experimental scheduler re-arms cron after dispatch success or terminal error. Resume falls back to fresh only for unknown session/no resume ref; a failed task does not thereby receive a documented retry-to-success policy.

retention.answer: The server event-log service prunes events older than 14 days or beyond 50,000 rows, on boot delay then every six hours. This is not a retention promise for comments, transcripts, artifacts or backups.

mutability.answer: The activity event store is pruned by that retention service; it is not an indefinite immutable audit ledger. Separate issue/comment edit-history behavior remains unestablished.

diffs.answer: The review guide directs the human to inspect changed files and Git diff alongside checks and artifacts. No tested revision-linked diff retention is claimed.

artifacts.answer: Per-issue offers attach durable evidence for review, with artifact navigation in the issue. A six-task review fixture and queue-level artifact coverage were not tested.

request_changes.answer: Offers provide a send-back feedback action that keeps the issue open and conveys the mismatch to the agent; batch request-changes semantics were not tested.

next_actions.answer: Review guidance gives merge versus feedback actions after checking evidence. Shipping remains an experimental path, and no batch-effort measurements were run.

tunnels.answer: Remote access uses an operator-configured TLS route, supported tunnel or private Tailscale network; daemons connect outbound and need no public inbound ports.

lifetime.answer: One-time machine pairing grants expire after one hour. This does not establish a per-command approval lifetime.
